title: What If It Rained Glass Sideways? One Planet May

scenes.text: What if it rained glass, sideways, at thousands of miles an hour? One planet possibly does.
The planet is HD 189733b, 63 light-years away, orbiting closer to its star than Mercury does to the Sun.
Its day side reaches nearly 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough for silicates, the stuff of glass, to turn to vapor.
Winds there reach about 4,500 miles an hour, so any droplets that form would be blown sideways, not down.
Tiny glass droplets would scatter blue light, which could explain why Hubble saw a deep cobalt-blue world.
So the prettiest planet ever photographed may have weather made of flying glass.
